title: The Beetle

full_text:
The emperor's war horse was shod with golden shoes because of its heroism in battle. The black dung-beetle, crawling out of the stable straw, held out his thin legs to the blacksmith: "Gold shoes for me also! I am just as noble as the horse!"

The blacksmith laughed and tossed him into the manure. Insulted, the beetle flew into the wide world, boasting to frogs, caterpillars, and hens that he was an imperial aristocrat traveling incognito.

Tossed by storms, stuck in clay pots, and nearly drowned in a tub, he finally crawled back into the emperor's stable, climbing onto the back of the golden-shod horse.

"Ah!" said the beetle with immense pride. "The emperor rides upon the horse, and the horse carries me! The entire empire rests upon my shoulders!"
moral: Pompous self-importance in insignificant beings is the height of comic delusion.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Beetle"?
options: Andersen's tales teach compassion, resilience, and Christian hope
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof

options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
